audit.why: 53.31% over 257 games and both sources agree exactly, so FAV at 7/10 is right. Karma has no dash and no blink — Inspire's move speed is her whole disengage — so once Sejuani closes, the CC chain is unanswerable. The difficulty sits in surviving the ranged phase, which is what the page says.

audit.whatIsWrong: win[3] and phases[3].side both say Karma for Levels 4-5, but three separate fields describe that stage as Sejuani's. mid opens 'Levels 4-5 flip the script as soon as your W is maxed'. spikes[1] says any Karma who steps past the wave 'gets punished by a full Q-W-E CC chain'. whys[3] says 'every step-up she takes into slow range is a free Frost stack into Permafrost stun — punish'.
audit.why: Winter's Wrath drops from 9 seconds to 5 as it maxes, which is the actual mechanism the prose is describing: at rank 5 Sejuani can re-apply Frost stacks faster than Karma's 9-to-5-second Inner Flame can trade back, and Permafrost costs 20 mana on a 1.5-second cooldown so the stun is always available once the stacks exist. The page already reached the right conclusion in prose and then scored the stage against it.
audit.corrected: Levels 4-5 moved to Sejuani on win[3] and phases[3].side, with phases[3].why rewritten to state the W cooldown that causes the flip.

audit.whatIsWrong: whys[0] and early call Sejuani's passive a 'Permafrost shield' and describe Karma popping it. Fury of the North grants Frost Armor — armour and magic resist plus immunity to slows — not a shield, and Permafrost is her 560-range E stun. The slow immunity is never mentioned even though Inner Flame is a slow, and nothing on the page connects Gathering Fire to the poke.
audit.why: Three things change how the lane is played. Frost Armor is resistances, so poke reduces its value rather than popping it like a shield. The immunity means Inner Flame's slow does not stop her walk-up while it holds — which is how she closes on a champion with no dash. And Gathering Fire means every damaging ability Karma lands shortens her Mantra cooldown, so poke you eat is not just HP, it is Mantra uptime; dodging is how you keep her ultimate off the field.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor named correctly and described as resistances in whys[0] and early; the slow immunity against Inner Flame is stated in early and wants.foe[0]; the Gathering Fire consequence is in wants.you[1] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: loading, report[5].t and breakdown.cooldowns all build the green light on 'Focused Resolve down' with no number, and mid says to break the tether with Q without saying what makes that work.
audit.why: Focused Resolve is a flat 12 seconds at every rank with a 675-range tether, and Arctic Assault charges 650 — so charging directly away from her is enough distance to break the link before the root lands. Mantra is 40 seconds at rank 1, but Gathering Fire shortens it on every damaging hit, so it is a budget she refills off you rather than a fixed timer.
audit.corrected: 12s and the 675-versus-650 range arithmetic added to mid, breakdown.cooldowns, report[5].t and loading; Mantra's 40s and its Gathering Fire refund stated in wants.you[1] and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal timing anywhere, despite Karma having a heal on her kit.
audit.why: Riot's Focused Resolve text: 'Mantra Bonus: Karma strengthens the link, healing herself and extending the root duration.' In the extended trades this page tells Sejuani to seek from level 4 onward, that heal is what undoes the chip damage.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds timing added to wants.you[2].

notes: Both win-rate sources agree exactly for Karma (53.31, 257 games), so nothing here rested on the source conflict affecting other matchups in this slice. Several fields I did not open still say 'Permafrost shield' or 'passive Permafrost' for Fury of the North, and phases[2].why calls Karma 'his'/'him'. Whether Arctic Assault's 650-unit charge reliably clears the 675 tether depends on your starting separation, which the kit files cannot settle — the page states the two ranges and lets the player judge, rather than promising the break.
